body.p: You can add comments to selected content in Markdown documents, reply to existing comments, edit your own comments, and remove comments. You can also manage all the comments of a document from the Review view. The comments are saved in the document as HTML comments, so the Markdown content itself remains unchanged. Each comment is attached to selected content and records the author's name and the time it was added. The author name is specified in the Review preferences page.

section.title: Adding a Comment
section.p:
To add a comment:
Select the content that you want to comment on. You can add a comment only to selected content.
Select the Add Comment action from the Markdown toolbar, contextual menu, or Document Markdown menu.
Type the comment in the dialog box that opens and click OK.

The commented content is highlighted, and a marker appears in the vertical stripe on the right side of the editor. Hover over the commented content or its marker to display the comment, its author, and the time it was added. Comments are rendered using the colors configured for comments in Author mode on the Review preferences page.

section.title: Replying to a Comment
section.p: To reply to a comment, place the cursor in the commented content, right-click, and select Add Reply from the contextual menu. The resulting dialog box displays the comment you are replying to, followed by its existing replies, so you can check where your reply is added. Replies are displayed with the comment when you hover over the commented content. You cannot reply to a comment that is marked as done.

section.title: Editing or Showing a Comment
section.p: To edit a comment, place the cursor in the commented content, right-click, and select Edit Comment from the contextual menu. As in Author mode, you can edit only comments that you added and that are not marked as done. Otherwise, the action is named Show Comment and it displays the comment without allowing changes. If a comment that you added already has replies, it is also only displayed along with a button that lets you to reply to it. Editing a comment preserves the time when it was added.

section.title: Removing a Comment
section.p: To remove a comment, place the cursor in the commented content, right-click, and select Remove Comment from the contextual menu. The comment and all its replies are removed. If several comments have been added to the same content, the innermost comment is removed.
If you delete all the content to which a comment was added, the comment is also removed.
section.note: Adding, editing, and removing comments and replies, as well as marking comments as done, can be undone and redone, just like any other editing action.

section.title: Managing Comments in the Review View
section.p: The Review view displays all comments in the current Markdown document, with each comment followed by its replies, as it does for comments in Author mode. To open the view, select the Manage reviews action from the Markdown toolbar, the contextual menu, or the Document Markdown menu.

The view and editor are synchronized. When you select a comment in the view, the commented content is selected in the editor. When you place the cursor within commented content, its comment is selected in the view.

The view offers the following features:
A filter field at the top of the view that displays only comments that contain the typed text in the author name, comment text, or commented content. If any comment in a thread matches, the entire thread is displayed. Typing an author name between quotation marks (for example, "john") displays only threads that contain comments by that exact author.
Previous and Next buttons that navigate through the comments.
A Settings menu that includes the Show review time option and the Sort by date submenu (Oldest to newest, Newest to oldest, No sorting). These settings are shared with the Review view in Author mode.
Double-click a comment or press Enter to edit or show it. Press Delete to remove the selected comments.

The following actions are available in the contextual menu of the view:
Edit Comment / Show Comment Edits or displays the selected comment, according to the same rules as in the editor.
Add Reply Adds a reply to the thread of the selected comment. Not available for comments marked as done.
Mark as Done Marks the comment thread (the comment and all its replies) as done. If it is already marked as done, marks it as not done. Comments marked as done are grayed out in the view and can no longer be edited.
Remove Comment(s) Removes the selected comments. Removing a comment also removes its replies, while removing a reply keeps the comment it replies to.
Remove all comments Removes all the comments from the document.
Show only reviews by '<author name>' Filters the view to show only comment threads that contain comments by the author of the selected comment.

section.title: How Comments Are Saved
section.p: The comments are saved in the Markdown document as pairs of HTML comments placed around the commented content. For example:
section.codeblock: Some <!--oxy_comment_start author="john" timestamp="20260908T161113+0300" comment="Please review"-->commented<!--oxy_comment_end--> text.
section.p: The editor does not display these HTML comments. Instead, it displays highlights over the commented content. If a comment starts or ends at the beginning of a line, its HTML comment is saved on a separate line. A comment marked as done is saved with a flag="done" attribute, and a comment that has replies is saved with an id attribute, referenced by the parentID attribute of its replies.

If a comment starts or ends at the boundary of a table row (for example, when you comment on entire table rows), its HTML comment is saved inside the nearest table cell, so the table structure is not broken.

section.title: Comments in the Preview Pane
section.p: The comments are also displayed in the DITA, XDITA, and HTML tabs of the Markdown Preview pane, in the same way as comments are displayed in Author mode. The preview is refreshed when you add, edit, or remove a comment. Each author's comments are rendered with the same color in the editor and in the preview, and colors are assigned to authors in the same way as in Author mode.

section.title: Turning Off Comments
section.p: You can turn off comments by deselecting the Enable comments option on the Markdown preferences page. When comments are turned off, you cannot add comments, HTML comments already in a document are displayed in the editor as regular content, and comments are not displayed in the Preview pane.
